title: Candidate 72hr Job Trial Kit — Async Task + Evaluation
content:
Purpose and high-level guidance:

This kit is a standardized 72-hour asynchronous job trial template for mid-senior IC technical hires (IC3–IC5). Goal: give candidates a realistic, time-boxed slice of our day-to-day work without requiring live pairing. Use this when: final stage interviewers want to validate execution and problem decomposition on a small, scoped piece of product work; when calendar coordination is difficult; or when we need a take-home that is more structure than a traditional code kata.

Key principles:
- Respect candidate time: 72 hours total, expected ~6–10 hours of focused work.
- Compensate: recommended $200 USD stipend for trials longer than 4 hours or for roles at L4+ (check local legal).
- IP & confidentiality: include a brief IP clause and a link to the standard candidate NDA in the submission instructions.
- Fairness: provide a rubric and example deliverables so assessors grade consistently. Avoid open-ended prompts that advantage those with product-context knowledge.

When not to use this kit:
- Early funnel screens (phone screens, take-home <60m).
- Roles that require live collaboration skills (senior infra on-call simulations) — prefer a short live pairing.
- When the candidate expresses strong preference not to do take-homes.

Structure (what we send the candidate):
1) Welcome brief (1 paragraph) that orients candidate to the exercise and makes clear that partial submissions are fine.
2) Problem statement (clear, scoped).
3) Acceptance criteria (bullet list).
4) Suggested deliverables (code sandbox link, readme, short writeup, tests).
5) Submission instructions (how to share work, deadline window / timezone guidance).
6) Legal/compensation note and contact person.

Sample problem (engineer — infra/runtime focus):
Title: "Reduce tail latency for small-chat workloads in a simulated inference pool"
Problem (short): We provide a lightweight simulator repository (link) that models request flows with variable token lengths and a naive request router. Your task: implement a small router heuristic and a micro-caching layer that reduces median and 95th percentile latency on the provided scenarios. Keep changes isolated to the provided modules.
Acceptance criteria (defensive, measurable):
- Implement router.strategy() that chooses either FIFO, small-first (prioritize requests with short max_tokens), or cost-aware (prefer fewer tokens).
- Add a KV-prefix cache API with put/get semantics and LRU eviction (configurable size).
- Write unit tests demonstrating correctness of the cache and router decisions in two scenarios (short-heavy and long-heavy workloads).
- Submit a 1-page README describing your approach, trade-offs, and one short experiment result (median and p95 latency before/after using provided harness).

Suggested deliverables (what we expect to receive):
- Git patch or GitHub repo with commit history.
- README.md (approach, perf numbers, run instructions).
- Minimal automated test(s).
- Optional: small script to reproduce perf numbers; if long-running, run on the included small data sample.

Evaluation rubric (single-page scoring we send to interviewers):
Scoring scale per dimension: 1 (insufficient) — 3 (meets bar) — 5 (exceeds). Total possible: 25. Pass threshold: >= 15 with no 1s in "collaboration" or "signal clarity".
- Problem decomposition & scope control (1–5): Did the candidate break the work into clear steps and avoid overengineering?
- Correctness & tests (1–5): Do delivered code and tests show they solved the stated problem?
- Engineering craft & code clarity (1–5): Readability, modularity, appropriate abstractions, helpful comments.
- Trade-offs & communication (1–5): README explains why choices were made and what was not done and why.
- Results & signal (1–5): Are performance numbers sensible and replicate the claim? Is there a clear delta?

Calibration notes for assessors:
- We prioritize concise, correct solutions over overly complex ones. A minimal, well-tested implementation with clear measurements beats a large un-runnable prototype.
- If candidate misses an acceptance criterion due to a time constraint but the design explains how they'd finish, consider partial credit rather than flat fail.
- All assessors must attach a 3–5 sentence evidence note (what you saw and why you scored).

Interviewer/assessor workflow and timeline (People Ops + Hiring Manager):
- Day 0: People Ops sends the kit + repo link + consent + NDA + stipend info. Candidate has 72 hours but can request an extension (one 48h extension allowed).
- Day 4: Candidate submits. People Ops acknowledges receipt and confirms stipend eligibility.
- Day 5–7: Two assessors (hiring manager + cross-team engineer) review independently using the rubric and fill the "evidence note".
- Day 7–8: Assembled feedback call / sync between assessors to reconcile scores. One assessor writes the hiring recommendation with explicit tie-break guidance.

Assessor checklist (quick):
- Run the code (clone, run tests).
- Confirm README contains run instructions and basic perf reproduction.
- Score each rubric dimension and write the evidence note (3–5 sentences).
- Flag any potential plagiarism or copied solutions.
- Time spent: target 60–90 minutes per assessor.

People Ops checklist for sending the trial (template):
- [ ] Confirm role and level with hiring manager (expected scope).
- [ ] Attach role-specific acceptance criteria (pre-filled).
- [ ] Include stipend amount and instructions for payment process.
- [ ] Add NDA link and IP blurb.
- [ ] Provide sample solution outline to reviewer guide (not shared with candidate).

Candidate-facing example README snippet (we send this as a template):
"What we care about:
- A working, well-tested minimal solution we can run quickly.
- Clear explanation of tradeoffs and what you'd do next in productizing the work.
- Honesty about time spent and what was not completed.

What to include in your submission:
- README.md with approach and perf numbers
- Link to code (GitHub, zip or gist)
- Any small scripts to reproduce results
- Short note: estimated time spent and anything you’d like us to know
"

Legal & compliance (short):
- Provide link to short candidate NDA. Use the standard company candidate NDA template (People Ops will attach).
- Stipend process: candidate supplies invoice or payment info; People Ops triggers expense within 5 business days of receipt.
- IP: specify that code submitted for trial is used for evaluation only; candidates may request deletion after decision. If candidate becomes an employee, standard employment IP assignment will apply.

Risk mitigation and fairness steps:
- Provide sample seed data and a light-weight simulator so candidates don’t need Redwood-specific infra.
- Offer an alternate short live pairing if candidate needs accommodation.
- Avoid linking to internal docs or closed-source resources.
- Track aggregated score distributions quarterly to detect systemic bias in trial difficulty.

Appendix: common pitfalls and assessor tips (bullet list):
- Don’t penalize for missing optional optimizations if core acceptance criteria are met.
- Watch for "copy-paste" solutions from public repos — flag and discuss with People Ops.
- Prefer incremental commits showing a working baseline rather than a single giant patch.

Contact and next steps:
- People Ops owner: Priya Nair (pri@redwood.ai) — questions about timers, stipend, or accommodations.
- Hiring manager template message to candidate (copy/paste ready) included in People Ops send flow.

This document is intended to be a living kit — please leave review comments in the linked Confluence page and note any repeated assessor confusion so the template can be improved.
